info.title: BillionSend API
info.description: Send and receive email, manage contacts and broadcasts, and read delivery events and statistics. Authenticate with a `bs_` API key sent as a Bearer token.

signing_secret.description: New secret to sign with: whsec_ followed by base64 of 24-64 bytes. Omit to mint one.

overlap_hours.description: Hours the previous secret keeps signing alongside the new one (default 24, max 72). Every delivery in the window carries both signatures, so a receiver holding either verifies; 0 drops the old secret at once.

record.description: Which record this is: DKIM, SPF (the MAIL FROM MX and TXT rows), DMARC, Tracking (the tracking subdomain's CNAME, present once a tracking subdomain is set), Unsubscribe (the unsubscribe subdomain's CNAME, present once an unsubscribe subdomain is set to a label other than the tracking one) or Receiving (the MX inbound mail needs, present while receiving is enabled; it reads verified only when it is among the domain's lowest-numbered MX records). Only the DKIM and SPF rows gate sending: the domain verifies once DKIM and the MAIL FROM pair verify. Add every record listed: mail whose MAIL FROM records are missing goes out with the provider's own return path, and DMARC still aligns on DKIM.

status.description: not_started | pending | verified | failed. DKIM and SPF rows combine public DNS with the provider's verification: found in DNS but not yet confirmed reads pending, a different published value reads failed, no record reads not_started. DMARC reads verified when a policy covers the domain — its own or a parent domain's (see inherited_from) — and not_started when none does. Tracking and Unsubscribe read verified once their CNAME resolves and its certificate is issued, pending until then, and failed when it did not activate within 72 hours.

live.description: What public DNS answers for this record right now: found, missing, mismatch (a different value is published) or unknown (the lookup did not conclude). Omitted when no live check ran (the create response).

detail.description: One sentence explaining a row that is not verified: found but awaiting the provider, the value that is published instead, no record at the name, or which parent DMARC policy covers the domain. Omitted when there is nothing to add.

inherited_from.description: DMARC only: the _dmarc name whose policy covers this domain when it has no record of its own (RFC 7489 organizational-domain fallback).

policy.description: DMARC only, alongside inherited_from: the inherited policy's p= value.

region.description: The SES region the domain sends from, one of the regions this deployment serves (the values listed here); without one, the first listed. Any other region is rejected with 422. Echoed back as the domain's region.

custom_return_path.description: The MAIL FROM (return-path) label, fixed when the domain is added: it cannot be changed later (delete and re-add the domain). The MAIL FROM host is `<label>-<region>.<domain>` (e.g. `bounce-us-east-2`), and records lists its MX and TXT. Defaults to `bounce`, not `send`, so a domain that still sends through another provider whose return path is `send` keeps its bounces working while both send.

open_tracking.description: Inject a tracking pixel served from the tracking host and record email.opened events. Off by default.

click_tracking.description: Rewrite links to redirect through the tracking host and record email.clicked events. Off by default.

tracking_subdomain.description: DNS label of the domain's own tracking host, e.g. "links" for links.<domain>. Optional: without one, tracked links use the shared tracking host. Setting it adds a Tracking CNAME to records[] (point it at the given value, DNS only); its certificate is issued automatically once it resolves, the Tracking record then reads verified, and links go through it from then on. A subdomain that does not activate within 72 hours reads failed; send the same tracking_subdomain again to retry.

unsubscribe_subdomain.description: BillionSend extension: DNS label of the domain's own unsubscribe host, e.g. "unsubscribe" for unsubscribe.<domain>. Optional: without one, unsubscribe links (and the List-Unsubscribe header) use the shared unsubscribe host. Setting it adds an Unsubscribe CNAME to records[] (point it at the given value, DNS only); its certificate is issued automatically once it resolves, the Unsubscribe record then reads verified, and unsubscribe links go through it from then on. The same label as tracking_subdomain is allowed: one host then serves both and records[] shows one row. A subdomain that does not activate within 72 hours reads failed; send the same unsubscribe_subdomain again to retry. Kept apart from tracking_subdomain because ad blockers filter tracking hosts by name.

receiving.description: Inbound mail for every address at the domain (a catch-all), readable at /emails/receiving and announced by the email.received webhook. A domain that already has mailboxes is best received on a subdomain (inbound.example.com): the Receiving MX would take their mail.

Only the DKIM and SPF rows gate sending: the domain verifies once DKIM and the MAIL FROM pair verify. Add every record listed: mail whose MAIL FROM records are missing goes out with the provider's own return path, and DMARC still aligns on DKIM.

status.description: not_started | pending | verified | failed. DKIM and SPF rows combine public DNS with the provider's verification: found in DNS but not yet confirmed reads pending, a different published value reads failed, no record reads not_started. DMARC reads verified when a policy covers the domain — its own or a parent domain's (see inherited_from) — and not_started when none does. Tracking and Unsubscribe read verified once their CNAME resolves and its certificate is issued, pending until then, and failed when it did not activate within 72 hours.

get.description: Mail received at the team's receiving domains and inboxes, newest first (`after` pages toward older mail), with cursor pagination. Needs a full access key; a domain-scoped key lists mail addressed to its domain only, an inbox-scoped key mail delivered into its inbox. Mail held for screening or in quarantine is left out unless a full access key asks for it (include_quarantined, quarantined). With wait, the request is held until matching mail arrives (long-poll). The inbox_id filter takes an inbox ID or its email address, as the /inboxes/{inbox_id} paths do. An inbox the key can't reach answers 404 at once, without waiting; an inbox-scoped key naming another inbox gets 403 restricted_api_key. Everything in a received email was written by whoever sent it, so its HTML is safe to show only in a sandbox.
